title: It’s not an election without an election prognostication contest
summary: Crystal ball? Tea leaves? Actual scientific surveys? Just your own obsessive knowledge of Maryland politics? Whatever your preferred method of predicting the political future, dust it off: Maryland Matters' election contest is back.
content:
by Maryland Matters Staff, Maryland Matters June 16, 2026

by Maryland Matters Staff, Maryland Matters June 16, 2026

Tired of slick mailers stuffing your mailbox, attack ads polluting the airwaves, and unceasing texts begging for campaign cash? Don’t worry, the end is near: The Maryland primaries are just a week away, on June 23.

But not everything associated with the political season has to be unpleasant. For one thing, it’s time to exercise your sacred constitutional rights as voters – before they’re stripped away. And even more fun, it’s time to test your knowledge and compete against your fellow Maryland Matters readers.

That’s right, it’s time to enter the Maryland Matters 2026 primary election challenge.

As always, we’re asking you to handicap several Maryland primaries, and we’ll throw you a few tie-breaking bonus questions. We’ll tally the points, the winner gets to choose between prizes: lunch with the Maryland Matters staffer of your choice, or a States Newsroom tote bag — hey, public broadcasting does it, why not us? — with swag.

Entering is simple: Please email your contest answers to electioncontestmm@gmail.com. The deadline for entries is 8 p.m. on Monday, June 22 – 24 hours before the polls close. Good luck with your entries – and please invite your friends to participate!

1) Who will win the Republican primary for governor ? __________

2) In 2002, Robert Fustero, a grocery store clerk, stunned the political world by taking 20% of the vote against then-Lt. Gov. Kathleen Kennedy Townsend in the Democratic primary for governor. This year, another political unknown, physician Eric Felber, is challenging Gov. Wes Moore (D) in the Democratic primary for governor. Yes or no – will Felber cross the Fustero Line in this year’s primary? __________

The candidates, the ballot measures, and the tools you need to cast your vote.

3) Who will win the Democratic primary in the 6th congressional district? __________

4) Who will win the Republican primary there? __________

5) Who will win the Democratic primary in the 5th congressional district? __________

6) Who will finish sixth in that 24-person primary? __________

7) Who will win the Democratic primary for Anne Arundel County executive? __________

8) Who will win the Democratic primary for Baltimore County executive? __________

9) Who will win the Republican primary for Harford County executive? __________

10) Who will win the Democratic primary for Howard County executive? __________

11) Who will win the Democratic primary for Montgomery County executive? __________

12) Three incumbent state’s attorneys face tough primaries this month: Scott Shellenberger (D) in Baltimore County, Anne Colt Leitess (D) in Anne Arundel County and Tara Jackson (D) in Prince George’s County. Name which ones, if any, will lose their primaries. __________

13) Two men named Kevin Ford are running in state Senate primaries: A Democrat named Kevin Ford in Prince George’s County’s District 24, and a Republican named Kevin Ford in the 42nd District, which takes in parts of Baltimore and Carroll counties. Will either of these Kevins win their primaries, and if so, which? __________

14) Who will win the 41st District Democratic Senate primary in Baltimore City between Sen. Dalya Attar and Del. Malcolm Ruff? __________

15) Who will win the Republican primary for House of Delegates in District 1A in Garrett County? __________

16) Sen. Nancy King (D-Montgomery) and two of the three delegates in District 39 are trying to knock off two-term Del. Gabriel Acevero (D) in their district, by supporting a challenger, Gaithersburg City Councilmember Robert Wu. Will they succeed? __________

17) Will Sen. King survive her own primary challenge? __________

18) Will any other state senators lose in the primary? If so, which ones? __________

19) Who will win the three-way Democratic primary for president of the Charles County Commission? __________

20) Who will win the Republican primary for Frederick County executive, Diane Fouche or William Holtzinger? __________

1) Who will win the Democratic state Senate primary in the 36th District for the right to take on Senate Minority Leader Steve Hershey (R) this fall, Nivek Johnson or John Queen?

2) What percentage of the vote will Baltimore City Councilmember Mark Conway (D) win in his bid to topple U.S. Rep. Kweisi Mfume (D)? Come within 2 points of predicting it correctly and you’ll win a point. __________

3) What percentage of the vote will tour boat captain Bobby LaPin (D) win in his bid to oust Senate President Bill Ferguson (D) in Baltimore City? Come within 2 points of predicting it correctly and you’ll win a point. __________
